subject: Medicine
summary: PCOS is a common endocrine disorder in reproductive‑age women, defined by excess androgens, irregular menses, and ovarian cysts. It causes infertility, metabolic issues, and hirsutism.

sections.p: PCOS is diagnosed when two of three features are present: clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, oligo/anovulation, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, after excluding other causes.
b: Polycystic ovaries: >12 follicles 2–9 mm or >10 cm volume

sections.p: Severity is staged by the Rotterdam criteria and the NIH 2003 criteria. A simple staging uses the number of cysts and androgen level.
b: Stage I: mild hirsutism, few cysts
Stage II: moderate hirsutism, many cysts
Stage III: severe hirsutism, many cysts and metabolic derangements

sections.p: The exact cause is unknown; most likely a combination of genetic predisposition and insulin resistance leading to hyperandrogenism.
b: Insulin resistance: hyperinsulinemia stimulates ovarian androgen production

sections.p: Women present with irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, weight gain, and infertility. Metabolic signs include acne, acneiform rash, and darkening of skin.
Investigations confirm diagnosis, exclude mimics, and assess complications.

t.b: Suggests PCOS; normal in other causes

sections.p: Complications include endometrial hyperplasia, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and infertility. Red flags need urgent care.
Treat underlying insulin resistance, control androgen excess, and manage menstrual irregularity. Lifestyle first, then pharmacology.
Regular monitoring of metabolic parameters and menstrual regularity is essential. Prevention focuses on early lifestyle changes.
b: Annual fasting glucose and lipid profile

sections.p: Conditions that mimic PCOS include congenital adrenal hyperplasia, androgen‑producing tumors, thyroid disorders, and hyperprolactinemia.
Low‑grade hyperandrogenism can be missed; ultrasound may be normal in early disease; insulin tests vary with fasting state.
b: Serum testosterone may be normal in mild cases

sections.p: Seek urgent care for severe abdominal pain, heavy bleeding, or signs of endometrial cancer.

t.b: Weight loss improves insulin sensitivity but often needs medication for ovulation
